<file>
00001| ---
00002| title: updateTag
00003| description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| `updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
00007| 
00008| This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.
00009| 
00010| ## Usage
00011| 
00012| `updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.
00013| 
00014| If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.
00015| 
00016| > **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.
00017| 
00018| ## Parameters
00019| 
00020| ```tsx
00021| updateTag(tag: string): void;
00022| ```
00023| 
00024| - `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to update. Must not exceed 256 characters. This value is case-sensitive.
00025| 
00026| Tags must first be assigned to cached data. You can do this in two ways:
00027| 
00028| - Using the [`next.tags`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) option with `fetch` for caching external API requests:
00029| 
00030| ```tsx
00031| fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })
00032| ```
00033| 
00034| - Using [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside cached functions or components with the `'use cache'` directive:
00035| 
00036| ```tsx
00037| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00038| 
00039| async function getData() {
00040|   'use cache'
00041|   cacheTag('posts')
00042|   // ...
00043| }
00044| ```
00045| 
00046| ## Returns
00047| 
00048| `updateTag` does not return a value.
00049| 
00050| ## Differences from revalidateTag
00051| 
00052| While both `updateTag` and `revalidateTag` invalidate cached data, they serve different purposes:
00053| 
00054| - **`updateTag`**:
00055|   - Can only be used in Server Actions
00056|   - Next request waits for fresh data (no stale content served)
00057|   - Designed for read-your-own-writes scenarios
00058| 
00059| - **`revalidateTag`**:
00060|   - Can be used in Server Actions and Route Handlers
00061|   - With `profile="max"` (recommended): Serves cached data while fetching fresh data in the background (stale-while-revalidate)
00062|   - With custom profile: Can be configured to any cache life profile for advanced usage
00063|   - Without profile: legacy behavior which is equivalent to `updateTag`
00064| 
00065| ## Examples
00066| 
00067| ### Server Action with Read-Your-Own-Writes
00068| 
00069| ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
00070| 'use server'
00071| 
00072| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00073| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00074| 
00075| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
00076|   const title = formData.get('title')
00077|   const content = formData.get('content')
00078| 
00079|   // Create the post in your database
00080|   const post = await db.post.create({
00081|     data: { title, content },
00082|   })
00083| 
00084|   // Invalidate cache tags so the new post is immediately visible
00085|   // 'posts' tag: affects any page that displays a list of posts
00086|   updateTag('posts')
00087|   // 'post-{id}' tag: affects the individual post detail page
00088|   updateTag(`post-${post.id}`)
00089| 
00090|   // Redirect to the new post - user will see fresh data, not cached
00091|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00092| }
00093| ```
00094| 
00095| ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
00096| 'use server'
00097| 
00098| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'

---
title: updateTag
description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
---

`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).

This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.

## Usage

`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.

If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.

> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.
